objective: Prove the odd-loop identity on every closed orientable surface with a cellularly embedded graph, for the twists a and a + PD(c); prove that a seam whose edges all join the loop's projection to its complement carries only the zero twist or PD(c); and that in a three-dimensional cubical complex such a seam carries only the zero twist unless the projection contains a closed surface.
status: Proved by LOOP-SHIELD-20261023-001C-P001 (V1 prose proof; 425 orientations from walks inside genus-2 line events, 300 random vertex sets and 200 tube loops checked; four controls rejected). On every closed orientable surface with a cellularly embedded graph, the wall involution pairs the line events of the twists q and q + PD(c), keeping every directed cycle, so their probabilities are equal; on a torus this is the odd-loop identity, and on genus g it pairs only these two of the 2^(2g-1) twists odd on c. The seams next to a vertex set carry exactly the duals of the classes of curves in its open star minus the graph on it (Lefschetz duality); for square tilings the open star retracts onto the graph plus a diagonal across each square with two opposite corners in the set, so next to a lone odd loop with no such square a seam carries only 0 or PD(c). In three dimensions the duality involves closed surfaces, and a set whose open star lies in a solid torus carries no seam class: no wall exists around a loop. A first version of the seam lemma using the graph alone was false (117 of 300 random sets) and is corrected.
title: Proof: the wall on closed surfaces
